correctness.rationale: Every graph input and 4096 vertex subsets is rebuilt by two independent component-search procedures. At all 12 integer cutoffs, 33,248 nonempty faces, 16,345 matching pairs, and 184,650 Hasse incidences are enumerated and checked for full acyclicity. Complete exact signed Morse boundary matrices have verified maximal rank and unit minors. The two-level CW complexes have critical cells only in degrees 0 and adjacent degrees >=4, so elementary integral homotopy cancellation proves the integral sphere-wedge sequence. Independently computed full mod-two simplicial boundary ranks agree, and decoded certificate replay succeeded.

originality.rationale: Targeted searches of the indexed mathematical-research corpus for the graph name, its vertex-to-triangle Petersen construction, the dissociation-complex alias, cutoff signatures, and relevant general classes found no claim implying the Tietze cutoff-by-cutoff integral homotopy types. The three primary texts were compared by actual hypotheses and conclusions: classified graph families or chordal/tree hypotheses exclude this nonchordal cubic graph. The closest recorded Petersen r=2 calculation is for a different graph and gives no transformation of the complexes. Bibliographic priority is conditional on the inspected record coverage; an equivalent unindexed result remains a stated risk.
residual_risks: An unpublished, unindexed or inaccessible Tietze-graph higher-independence calculation may exist.

The expected known r>=12 simplex case is not a novelty claim.

value.rationale: A natural, canonical twelve-vertex cubic graph obtained by triangle expansion of Petersen has its entire cutoff-indexed family of higher-independence complexes integrally classified. This reveals non-monotone sphere dimensions, a distinguished mixed-dimensional r=5 wedge, large r=6 and r=7 multiplicities, and a controlled final collapse. It is more than a routine endpoint or isolated numerical invariant; no unproved general theorem is asserted.
